A sore throat after drinking alcohol is  [Highlight start] usually caused by **dehydration, direct tissue irritation, or acid reflux** [Highlight end] , and it typically clears up within 24 to 48 hours.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXX4avjzfAZLvDIxRI7pkV1-VTLBRl42xG85ErD6eVxuqER_4kMKp80FZ9uCH4vTOLqS8Qw5z6oOFB08KTUOC_0QnzVJQ6iMnzWwJCXutGaO58wygtgahNRk2OC9l9S2GcRb_HdjVAIkUfscvcYIzOqlaj5)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXTTZKNFvxcaIZNgNUUxVqlp0oC5h75mzKuzBgdlcDBS7tH_OmoTOuCoLDvx6nYeyJzwtJOlhOsLuwC0IZ-WEiLa6pv3xzgBXUtG3RkLKAznfCk0ccTLg_uaAVhYGlsxPo7NaEqEa9d64AZ_r_NXa4ipXVaaO4Iae3)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXX9e9ZReVUUR9ZrHdtJVuf_mkYIQyKRlAgwEt3MbVAXvVPSX0Kzxj3so2fXyow9BAjaKMsVJy5umSyGd8yvtUABDBbQTvdEksSPtRS3VIEQhTQSMKWi0OXk07_gGr5WEksdzzA4AvTBAJrJHbhy-RhBEvQMAksu9k53NA)

### Common Causes

- **Dehydration:** Alcohol acts as a diuretic and dries out the mucous membranes in your mouth and throat, making them feel scratchy and raw.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1xb_fCIrRgeZ6ouH6fIG6G-S2tbubesj5ZguUCZBqg0-_-i0M1gHc55j_P3NFADTImsWFmIlwNgLh6-txGI_6Q95pZlOlMX27NdciAgLWkvpgYk_EiJMMuW1M64PWrmz_Q3L64naF4-ZO5BfPzm48ZLQUJYNqAE36RbsnSbQe9su)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXX4avjzfAZLvDIxRI7pkV1-VTLBRl42xG85ErD6eVxuqER_4kMKp80FZ9uCH4vTOLqS8Qw5z6oOFB08KTUOC_0QnzVJQ6iMnzWwJCXutGaO58wygtgahNRk2OC9l9S2GcRb_HdjVAIkUfscvcYIzOqlaj5)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXw2cLhz833MlpfSEri96pqaHLDM3d3ApQ7T0CcmhNa_eIPM66KHcai5AebNcYTQvtejnEPFRa6o9iOmdtJpL8EYt3YOY_Vn05cL7kHCUG1LHOxT9XtcQjdGcYPTEep_OtSeI9gCvl0CEguZAFPXBiowgH5iZ96oE)
- **Acid reflux:** Alcohol relaxes the valve between your stomach and esophagus, letting stomach acid irritate your throat lining.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF16sOFWKllEM07Ak_tro2eJNO01KQAMMBKmJrbnfofHRMoi5wD9WFJlJhFWjdgtmZysItrN_865WazqhxVmeELLDDaEcMpgyw0JIxkLKAYB8lANEtds6twVat73dM1kLtyOcw8w7CIjV2BgtFHlJJl5uFSvywHTI_1gNRyIey1q43KZmDk6RB)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXw2cLhz833MlpfSEri96pqaHLDM3d3ApQ7T0CcmhNa_eIPM66KHcai5AebNcYTQvtejnEPFRa6o9iOmdtJpL8EYt3YOY_Vn05cL7kHCUG1LHOxT9XtcQjdGcYPTEep_OtSeI9gCvl0CEguZAFPXBiowgH5iZ96oE)
- **Direct irritation and sensitivities:** Alcohol can directly inflame throat tissues. Sulfites, histamines, or carbonation in wine and beer can also trigger throat irritation or tightness in sensitive people.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXTTZKNFvxcaIZNgNUUxVqlp0oC5h75mzKuzBgdlcDBS7tH_OmoTOuCoLDvx6nYeyJzwtJOlhOsLuwC0IZ-WEiLa6pv3xzgBXUtG3RkLKAznfCk0ccTLg_uaAVhYGlsxPo7NaEqEa9d64AZ_r_NXa4ipXVaaO4Iae3)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiwEBxCJF16sOFWKllEM07Ak_tro2eJNO01KQAMMBKmJrbnfofHRMoi5wD9WFJlJhFWjdgtmZysItrN_865WazqhxVmeELLDDaEcMpgyw0JIxkLKAYB8lANEtds6twVat73dM1kLtyOcw8w7CIjV2BgtFHlJJl5uFSvywHTI_1gNRyIey1q43KZmDk6RB)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlgEBxCJF1zZ4jNLixTewLsTqk6OcnQYT1EsywWvRV6iNjsTbsiLyzNd1iLBrgnzh00WP9owVfHScu58fTgDD859bGbDCWYshas1a6YnGQaxCmdY3bkDSZhP5PeBbfXK2SazB6Uli8huYKcMc2BnaJCICAfPJ0oMTls6mJfZQlgAkkWY-GUIuW1Igni_wmaD26D_BOdDJhqg)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXw2cLhz833MlpfSEri96pqaHLDM3d3ApQ7T0CcmhNa_eIPM66KHcai5AebNcYTQvtejnEPFRa6o9iOmdtJpL8EYt3YOY_Vn05cL7kHCUG1LHOxT9XtcQjdGcYPTEep_OtSeI9gCvl0CEguZAFPXBiowgH5iZ96oE)
- **Strain and infections:** Talking loudly in noisy places strains vocal cords, while alcohol can temporarily lower immune defenses against viruses or bacteria. Most users on [Reddit](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmgEBxCJF15SPw4AyWKtOw7aAwAOea1WV9jVK6ScaKvFvbUkNXMdHn0zH_FR2Yj8h7Uuo0XbvQzs3hRNt_ss-hlUqjuo9kX2q1iHW6wdK6hF4Op54hV37-1SpELUbZT0y1oXktdFXkPTuthnJpQqrBvv2h9VjfyfEEnuYU_3ff34B35tAT2lK8bwxX9nNRv4HfOcIVWuXjm0I_pve) also note a consensus that reflux can drive sore throats and congestion after drinking, which often improves by cutting back or stopping alcohol.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXX4avjzfAZLvDIxRI7pkV1-VTLBRl42xG85ErD6eVxuqER_4kMKp80FZ9uCH4vTOLqS8Qw5z6oOFB08KTUOC_0QnzVJQ6iMnzWwJCXutGaO58wygtgahNRk2OC9l9S2GcRb_HdjVAIkUfscvcYIzOqlaj5)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXTTZKNFvxcaIZNgNUUxVqlp0oC5h75mzKuzBgdlcDBS7tH_OmoTOuCoLDvx6nYeyJzwtJOlhOsLuwC0IZ-WEiLa6pv3xzgBXUtG3RkLKAznfCk0ccTLg_uaAVhYGlsxPo7NaEqEa9d64AZ_r_NXa4ipXVaaO4Iae3)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1xb_fCIrRgeZ6ouH6fIG6G-S2tbubesj5ZguUCZBqg0-_-i0M1gHc55j_P3NFADTImsWFmIlwNgLh6-txGI_6Q95pZlOlMX27NdciAgLWkvpgYk_EiJMMuW1M64PWrmz_Q3L64naF4-ZO5BfPzm48ZLQUJYNqAE36RbsnSbQe9su)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESmgEBxCJF15SPw4AyWKtOw7aAwAOea1WV9jVK6ScaKvFvbUkNXMdHn0zH_FR2Yj8h7Uuo0XbvQzs3hRNt_ss-hlUqjuo9kX2q1iHW6wdK6hF4Op54hV37-1SpELUbZT0y1oXktdFXkPTuthnJpQqrBvv2h9VjfyfEEnuYU_3ff34B35tAT2lK8bwxX9nNRv4HfOcIVWuXjm0I_pve)

### Home Relief

- **Rehydrate:** Drink plenty of water or electrolyte fluids.
- **Soothe the throat:** Try warm tea with honey, warm saltwater gargles, lozenges, or ice chips.
- **Rest your voice and body:** Avoid more alcohol, smoking, and spicy or acidic foods while healing.
- **Be cautious with pain relievers:** Check with a doctor or pharmacist before taking acetaminophen or ibuprofen after drinking, as combining alcohol with certain over-the-counter medications can stress your liver or stomach.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXX9e9ZReVUUR9ZrHdtJVuf_mkYIQyKRlAgwEt3MbVAXvVPSX0Kzxj3so2fXyow9BAjaKMsVJy5umSyGd8yvtUABDBbQTvdEksSPtRS3VIEQhTQSMKWi0OXk07_gGr5WEksdzzA4AvTBAJrJHbhy-RhBEvQMAksu9k53NA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXX4avjzfAZLvDIxRI7pkV1-VTLBRl42xG85ErD6eVxuqER_4kMKp80FZ9uCH4vTOLqS8Qw5z6oOFB08KTUOC_0QnzVJQ6iMnzWwJCXutGaO58wygtgahNRk2OC9l9S2GcRb_HdjVAIkUfscvcYIzOqlaj5)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAES3AEBxCJF14kw0F2G0DeeFZpvufX73k8hHqy8gmQMfoMplkmet1OEkBB_XJ1sUhH_R7hj_BdB2-pXxQPYJyOd4xNMhRH5OVa_Pm5zTN-Kp72gaDbDxjWSxdcHga86TvN7rsVXqToGL3L4EJL8ZD6uFA5Nyw2Ga3PUZ9C9KyVUKcCxgrcHvBVfj8gpgr8q3E5zxwLfu6NEjObLCt6lLwSvml38YqW7QEgMtl4Enx64I2QEkMfEKbvGssjm_svRyl5CFT6pWzVgUh0cJOmPAZm9oM5O6_OKkGCj6B5vSDpL)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF1xb_fCIrRgeZ6ouH6fIG6G-S2tbubesj5ZguUCZBqg0-_-i0M1gHc55j_P3NFADTImsWFmIlwNgLh6-txGI_6Q95pZlOlMX27NdciAgLWkvpgYk_EiJMMuW1M64PWrmz_Q3L64naF4-ZO5BfPzm48ZLQUJYNqAE36RbsnSbQe9su)

### When to Seek Medical Care
Get evaluated by a doctor if your sore throat lasts more than a few days to a week, keeps getting worse, or comes with a fever, swollen glands, or frequent heartburn. Seek urgent care right away if you have trouble breathing, severe pain or trouble swallowing, drooling, or swelling in your neck or tongue.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXrjsp5aK4xTBFmludAA5cg6i6u43KZpNU5Sbm8_NwS1UkKrJPrbU0SipJeWgmvbJGFS9Ms1HDHSPXw-f5pH8q9-WBRA-l027Cj7qLt4-WE0F_C0WSq_pRDEOuouDkonVrDQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXTTZKNFvxcaIZNgNUUxVqlp0oC5h75mzKuzBgdlcDBS7tH_OmoTOuCoLDvx6nYeyJzwtJOlhOsLuwC0IZ-WEiLa6pv3xzgBXUtG3RkLKAznfCk0ccTLg_uaAVhYGlsxPo7NaEqEa9d64AZ_r_NXa4ipXVaaO4Iae3)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfwHEIkXX9e9ZReVUUR9ZrHdtJVuf_mkYIQyKRlAgwEt3MbVAXvVPSX0Kzxj3so2fXyow9BAjaKMsVJy5umSyGd8yvtUABDBbQTvdEksSPtRS3VIEQhTQSMKWi0OXk07_gGr5WEksdzzA4AvTBAJrJHbhy-RhBEvQMAksu9k53NA)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAES3AEBxCJF14kw0F2G0DeeFZpvufX73k8hHqy8gmQMfoMplkmet1OEkBB_XJ1sUhH_R7hj_BdB2-pXxQPYJyOd4xNMhRH5OVa_Pm5zTN-Kp72gaDbDxjWSxdcHga86TvN7rsVXqToGL3L4EJL8ZD6uFA5Nyw2Ga3PUZ9C9KyVUKcCxgrcHvBVfj8gpgr8q3E5zxwLfu6NEjObLCt6lLwSvml38YqW7QEgMtl4Enx64I2QEkMfEKbvGssjm_svRyl5CFT6pWzVgUh0cJOmPAZm9oM5O6_OKkGCj6B5vSDpL)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfAHEIkXXw2cLhz833MlpfSEri96pqaHLDM3d3ApQ7T0CcmhNa_eIPM66KHcai5AebNcYTQvtejnEPFRa6o9iOmdtJpL8EYt3YOY_Vn05cL7kHCUG1LHOxT9XtcQjdGcYPTEep_OtSeI9gCvl0CEguZAFPXBiowgH5iZ96oE)[[6]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXD14n1sJKXdVPrJRTgwK_329WIvPXvG-BV-lE8xQtFLWC0jac3wko9NWW0VCs7Rlo0GLQLrZPGV3yQWIf1J0PgiJ1qoStTPfwjy7zfoFBuA7mFwZ3N7RpmxhrTpPwe8MISwoQjGPi)For items.title: Common Causes
items.text: Dehydration: Alcohol acts as a diuretic and dries out the mucous membranes in your mouth and throat, making them feel scratchy and raw. Acid reflux: Alcohol relaxes the valve between your stomach and esophagus, letting stomach acid irritate your throat lining. Direct irritation and sensitivities: Alcohol can directly inflame throat tissues. Sulfites, histamines, or carbonation in wine and beer can also trigger throat irritation or tightness in sensitive people. Strain and infections: Talking loudly in noisy places strains vocal cords, while alcohol can temporarily lower immune defenses against viruses or bacteria. Most users on Reddit also note a consensus that reflux can drive sore throats and congestion after drinking, which often improves by cutting back or stopping alcohol.

items.title: Home Relief
items.text: Rehydrate: Drink plenty of water or electrolyte fluids. Soothe the throat: Try warm tea with honey, warm saltwater gargles, lozenges, or ice chips. Rest your voice and body: Avoid more alcohol, smoking, and spicy or acidic foods while healing. Be cautious with pain relievers: Check with a doctor or pharmacist before taking acetaminophen or ibuprofen after drinking, as combining alcohol with certain over-the-counter medications can stress your liver or stomach.
items.markdown:

- **Soothe the throat:** Try warm tea with honey, warm saltwater gargles, lozenges, or ice chips.

items.title: When to Seek Medical Care
items.text: Get evaluated by a doctor if your sore throat lasts more than a few days to a week, keeps getting worse, or comes with a fever, swollen glands, or frequent heartburn. Seek urgent care right away if you have trouble breathing, severe pain or trouble swallowing, drooling, or swelling in your neck or tongue.
